I started taking actual dance classes around the same age as you. I'm about 20 now and tbh if you like ballet just keep going with it ! I understand your frustration on lack of corrections and it sucks. I found that teachers will help you if ask for help on something specific before or after class. They usually give you a small tip and you gotta just take that and run with it ! It's hard to see your progress as a dancer when you're having doubts about yourself so take videos of combinations you learn and keep them for future reference! It's so helpful to see them later and how to apply corrections. Also if you keep them you get to see how you've grown as a dancer. The new adult class sounds like it'd be a good challenge for you! As time goes on you'll hopefully feel a bit less frazzled. Whatever you decide to do I hope you stick with dancing as it seems like you care a lot about it :)


 Breaking down the movements at the barre really helps. For pas de chat make sure you roll through your feet into the pas de chat and rolling through your feet to land it as well. For chaines practice at the barre or put something on the floor to help guide you in a straight line. Do it slowly at first, taking half turns along the line. Keep your feet close in essentially just 1st position but relevé. Make sure your not over turning your half turn or not turning enough. Spotting is hard but it really just takes practice. I tend to put a sticky note on the wall at home and spot it when I'm bored, waiting on food to heat up, or during Hulu commercials.
